trigger: Same dry-run of select_frozen_cohort(seed=100100) that surfaced the financing gap (see financing-evidence-ledger-05.json) showed the specific 120-event selected cohort would only contain 18 of the 20 single-asset issuers required, with 102 of the 120 selected candidates still single_asset_status=PENDING. This ledger records genuine per-issuer pipeline research (pre-event 10-K/10-KT 'Item 1. Business' overview) against 8 of those selected-but-unverified candidates, following the qualification discipline already established in single-asset-evidence-ledger-08.json (MDGL/resmetirom): count only a company whose pre-event filings show one meaningful active clinical-stage therapeutic asset, where any other named compound is explicitly framed as a preclinical/backup/potential program rather than a separate active development effort.

rows.evidence_summary: FY2020 10-K 'Item 1. Business' overview states the company's efforts are focused on 'our lead product candidate, SGT-001,' a Duchenne muscular dystrophy gene transfer candidate. A full-text search of the filing for the SGT-\d+ naming pattern returns only SGT-001; every other reference to 'other product candidates' is generic forward-looking-statement hedge language ('SGT-001 and our other product candidates, if approved') with no second candidate ever named anywhere in the document - the same pattern that qualified MDGL/resmetirom in single-asset-evidence-ledger-08.json.

FY2024 10-K 'Item 1. Business' overview explicitly describes the company as developing 'deramiocel and our other product candidates including our exosomes platform technology,' and separately details an active StealthX exosome R&D program with NIH/NIAID/DoD/JHU collaborations 'developing exosome-based vaccines and therapeutics for infectious disease.' Unlike the MDGL precedent (where the second compound was explicitly called only a potential backup), this is affirmatively described as a distinct, actively funded second platform, not a backup for deramiocel.

FY2023 10-K 'Item 1. Business' overview states the company is 'also developing AMX0114, an antisense oligonucleotide, for the treatment of people living with ALS' - a chemically distinct compound (ASO vs. the AMX0035 small-molecule combination) with its own development program, not merely AMX0035 studied in an additional indication (which would not disqualify single-asset status, as with Amylyx's own AMX0035-in-PSP/Wolfram-syndrome studies).

FY2019 10-K 'Item 1. Business' overview states the pipeline 'also includes CRB-4001, a 2nd generation, peripherally restricted cannabinoid receptor type 1 (CB1) inverse agonist designed to treat organ specific fibrotic liver diseases, such as nonalcoholic steatohepatitis' - a distinct compound with a distinct mechanism and distinct target indication from lenabasum, affirmatively named as part of the active pipeline.

FY2020 10-K 'Item 1. Business' overview states the company received IND clearance for both 'our lead oncology program, RTX-240, and our lead artificial antigen presenting cell (aAPC) program, RTX-321' during 2020, with both actively dosing/enrolling. Two separate, named, clinical-stage (IND-cleared) programs.

FY2023 10-K 'Item 1. Business' overview explicitly states the company's 'priorities [are] focused on the development and potential commercialization of our two clinical-stage assets, losmapimod and pociredir' - self-described as two assets in the filing's own language.

FY2021 10-K (fiscal year end Sept. 30) 'Overview and Strategy' states the company 'currently [has] two core programs and two seed programs,' with ANAVEX2-73 as lead compound and this candidate's own asset, ANAVEX3-71, as a separate core program - self-described multi-program pipeline, not a single-asset company.

FY2019 10-K states the company is 'also developing a next-generation p53 reactivator, APR-548, for potential use in multiple hematologic malignancy indications.' APR-548 was preclinical at the time (no clinical trials yet initiated) while APR-246 was in pivotal Phase 3, which is a closer call than the other DOES_NOT_QUALIFY rows in this batch - but APR-548 is affirmatively described as a distinct compound under active development ('next-generation... developing'), not framed as only a potential backup the way MDGL's second compound was in single-asset-evidence-ledger-08.json. Treated conservatively as DOES_NOT_QUALIFY rather than stretching the MDGL precedent.

promotion_boundary: Single-asset status alone does not establish final M7 eligibility. Historical universe, timestamp, financing, point-in-time evidence, concentration, eligible-registry and deterministic cohort-freeze checks remain mandatory. This batch closes 8 of the 102 selected-but-unverified candidates but only found one genuine QUALIFIES; the selected-cohort single-asset count moves from 18 to 19, still one short of the 20 requirement - more candidates need review.
